hints: To find the words, turn every character that is not a letter or an apostrophe into a space, then split: `"".join(c if c.isalpha() or c == "'" else " " for c in text.lower()).split()`.
`Counter.most_common` does not break ties alphabetically, so sort `counts.items()` yourself with `key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0])` and slice the first `n`.
requirements: `words(text: str) -> list[str]` lower-cases the text and keeps only runs of letters and apostrophes.
`top(text: str, n: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]` returns the `n` most common words; equal counts in alphabetical order.
Write at least four `assert` tests in a `test()` function, including an empty text.
stretch: Leave out common words (a list of "stop words" such as `the`, `a`, `and`) through an optional parameter.
